# 04 The shapes drawn with a curve

## Outcome

`A((Circle))`, `A(((Double)))` and `A[(Cylinder)]` draw the shapes they name. Every bracket
spelling Mermaid has for a node now draws.

## Why this ticket exists

The three curved shapes, and the last of the thirteen. A circle is the shape where
*fits-inside* costs the most — a label needs a circle whose diameter spans its diagonal, so a wide
label produces a very large node, and that is a real layout consequence rather than a rendering
detail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] All three parse to their `NodeShape` and draw with the label fitting inside.
- [x] **A circle's diameter accounts for the label's diagonal, not its width.** Assert it with a
      label wide enough that the difference is unmistakable, and state what a long label does to
      the node's size — if the honest answer is "it gets very large", say so rather than quietly
      capping it. If you do cap it, that is a decision to state and justify, not a default.
- [x] A double circle is visibly two rings, and both belong to the frame for styling — an author's
      `fill` must not paint only one of them. State what you did.
- [x] A cylinder's top ellipse is drawn; it is the shape board 4 measured as producing a rectangle
      labelled `(DB)`, so a test naming that history is worth having.
- [~] Board 4's `UNIMPLEMENTED_BRACKET_FORMS` — its **shape** half is gone and it is renamed
      `UNIMPLEMENTED_LABEL_FORMS`; the Markdown label row survives, because deleting the
      mechanism would turn it into a silent mis-render. Correct call. Originally: **empty and deleted**, along with its lookup
      and the diagnostics it produced. Grep to prove nothing refers to it.
- [x] Each shape still takes an author style and still animates.
- [x] Three corpus rows move to `supported`. `REJECTED` 23 → **20**; `SILENTLY_WRONG` untouched
      at **3**. **After this ticket no `fc-shape-*` row remains rejected** — confirm that by
      grepping the corpus, not by counting.

- [x] **The theme's coverage net is blind to your shapes until you widen it.**
      `theme/default.test.ts`'s "has a rule selecting every class the flowchart renderer emits"
      renders `EVERY_FLOWCHART_FEATURE`, which draws **only rectangles** — so a new `siren-*` class
      your shape emits would ship unthemed without failing anything. Add your shapes to that
      fixture if they emit any class the rect path does not, and say in your report whether they
      do. This matters most here because a multi-element frame is exactly where a second class
      gets invented.

- [x] **Found by ticket 02b.** `corpus.ts`'s `nodeStyle` and `nodeCenter` readers still query
      `rect.siren-node-frame`, so they silently return `""` or throw for a path-drawn node. No row
      uses them on a shaped node today, so nothing is wrong yet — but if you write a row that
      asserts styling or position on one of your shapes, widen them first rather than discovering
      it as a confusing empty string.

## On the ratchet numbers in this ticket

They are an **expectation, not a quota.** Ticket 01 found a real compatibility gap and declined to
fix it because adding a corpus row would have pushed `REJECTED` one above the number its ticket
named. That was an honest reading of a badly written instruction: the ratchet exists to stop
regressions, not to stop progress.

So: if you discover a gap, **add the row and say so**. `rejected` rising because a new gap was
measured is the same legitimate case as `silently-wrong` rising in board 4 — a measurement was
corrected, not code made worse. State which in your report, and move the literal to whatever the
suite actually produces.
